quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Sloth makes all Things difficult, but Industry all easy
quotes.translation: الكسل يجعل كل شيء صعبًا، والاجتهاد يجعل كل شيء سهلًا.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: He that riseth late, must trot all Day, and shall scarce overtake his Business at Night
quotes.translation: من يستيقظ متأخرًا يظل يركض طوال اليوم، وبالكاد يدرك عمله في الليل.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Laziness travels so slowly, that Poverty soon overtakes him
quotes.translation: الكسل يمشي ببطء شديد حتى يلحق به الفقر سريعًا.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Drive thy Business, let not that drive thee
quotes.translation: قُد عملك، ولا تدعه يقودك.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Early to Bed, and early to rise, makes a Man healthy, wealthy and wise
quotes.translation: النوم مبكرًا والاستيقاظ مبكرًا يجعلان المرء صحيحًا وغنيًا وحكيمًا.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Industry need not wish
quotes.translation: المجتهد لا يحتاج إلى التمنّي.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: He that lives upon Hope will die fasting
quotes.translation: من يعيش على الأمل وحده يموت جائعًا.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: There are no Gains, without Pains
quotes.translation: لا مكاسب بلا تعب.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: He that hath a Trade hath an Estate
quotes.translation: من يملك حرفة يملك ثروة.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Diligence is the Mother of Good luck
quotes.translation: الاجتهاد أبو الحظ السعيد.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: One To-day is worth two Tomorrows
quotes.translation: يوم واحد اليوم خير من غدَين.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Have you somewhat to do To-morrow, do it To-day
quotes.translation: إن كان لديك عمل غدًا، فأنجزه اليوم.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: constant Dropping wears away Stones
quotes.translation: قطرات الماء المتتابعة تثقب الحجر.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: little Strokes fell great Oaks
quotes.translation: الضربات الصغيرة تُسقط أشجار البلوط العظيمة.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Employ thy Time well if thou meanest to gain Leisure
quotes.translation: أحسِن استغلال وقتك إن أردت أن تنال الراحة.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: since thou art not sure of a Minute, throw not away an Hour
quotes.translation: ما دمت لست متأكدًا من دقيقة، فلا تُضيّع ساعة.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Keep thy Shop, and thy Shop will keep thee
quotes.translation: اعتنِ بمتجرك، يعتنِ بك متجرك.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: The Eye of a Master will do more Work than both his Hands
quotes.translation: عين صاحب العمل تُنجز أكثر مما تنجزه يداه.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: If you would be wealthy, think of Saving as well as of Getting
quotes.translation: إن أردت الثراء، ففكّر في الادخار كما تفكر في الكسب.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Temperance. Eat not to dullness; drink not to elevation.
quotes.translation: الاعتدال: لا تأكل حتى الخمول، ولا تشرب حتى السُّكر.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Silence. Speak not but what may benefit others or yourself; avoid trifling conversation.
quotes.translation: الصمت: لا تقل إلا ما ينفع غيرك أو ينفعك، وتجنّب الكلام التافه.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Order. Let all your things have their places; let each part of your business have its time.
quotes.translation: النظام: اجعل لكل شيء من أشيائك مكانًا، ولكل جزء من عملك وقتًا.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Resolution. Resolve to perform what you ought; perform without fail what you resolve.
quotes.translation: العزم: اعزم على أداء ما يجب عليك، وأدِّ ما عزمت عليه دون تقصير.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Frugality. Make no expense but to do good to others or yourself, i.e., waste nothing.
quotes.translation: الاقتصاد: لا تنفق إلا لخيرٍ لغيرك أو لنفسك؛ أي لا تُسرف في شيء.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Industry. Lose no time; be always employed in something useful; cut off all unnecessary actions.
quotes.translation: الاجتهاد: لا تُضِع وقتًا؛ كن دائمًا مشغولًا بشيء نافع، واقطع كل عمل لا ضرورة له.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Sincerity. Use no hurtful deceit; think innocently and justly, and, if you speak, speak accordingly.
quotes.translation: الصدق: لا تلجأ إلى خداع مؤذٍ؛ فكّر ببراءة وعدل، وإن تكلمت فتكلم بما يوافق ذلك.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Justice. Wrong none by doing injuries or omitting the benefits that are your duty.
quotes.translation: العدل: لا تظلم أحدًا بإيذائه، أو بإغفال ما يجب عليك من نفعه.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Moderation. Avoid extremes; forbear resenting injuries so much as you think they deserve.
quotes.translation: التوسط: تجنّب التطرف، ولا تُبالغ في الغضب من الإساءة بقدر ما تظن أنها تستحق.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Cleanliness. Tolerate no uncleanliness in body, clothes, or habitation.
quotes.translation: النظافة: لا تقبل أي قذارة في جسدك أو ثيابك أو مسكنك.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: Tranquillity. Be not disturbed at trifles, or at accidents common or unavoidable.
quotes.translation: السكينة: لا تضطرب للتوافه، ولا للحوادث المعتادة أو التي لا مفر منها.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Virtue name added before its precept as on the page.

quotes.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach.
quotes.translation: ذهبت إلى الغابة لأني أردت أن أعيش بوعي، وأواجه حقائق الحياة الأساسية فقط، وأرى إن كنت أستطيع أن أتعلم ما لديها لتعلّمني إياه.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.work: Walden, ch. 2 “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Our life is frittered away by detail.
quotes.translation: حياتنا تتبدد في التفاصيل.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.work: Walden, ch. 2 “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Let us spend one day as deliberately as Nature, and not be thrown off the track by every nutshell and mosquito's wing that falls on the rails.
quotes.translation: لنقضِ يومًا واحدًا بتأنٍّ مثل الطبيعة، دون أن تُخرجنا عن مسارنا قشرةُ جوزة أو جناح بعوضة يسقط على السكة.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.work: Walden, ch. 2 “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Time is but the stream I go a-fishing in.
quotes.translation: ما الوقت إلا نهر أذهب لأصطاد فيه.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.work: Walden, ch. 2 “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page. Dash normalized from the page.

quotes.text: Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me.
quotes.translation: الصباح هو حين أكون يقظًا ويكون في داخلي فجر.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.work: Walden, ch. 2 “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: To be awake is to be alive.
quotes.translation: أن تكون يقظًا يعني أن تكون حيًّا.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.work: Walden, ch. 2 “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Why should we live with such hurry and waste of life?
quotes.translation: لماذا نعيش بكل هذه العجلة وهذا الهدر للحياة؟
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.work: Walden, ch. 2 “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Sell your clothes and keep your thoughts.
quotes.translation: بِع ثيابك واحتفظ بأفكارك.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Things do not change; we change.
quotes.translation: الأشياء لا تتغير؛ نحن الذين نتغير.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Do not trouble yourself much to get new things, whether clothes or friends.
quotes.translation: لا تُتعب نفسك كثيرًا في الحصول على أشياء جديدة، سواء أكانت ثيابًا أم أصدقاء.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Let him step to the music which he hears, however measured or far away.
quotes.translation: دعه يمشِ على إيقاع الموسيقى التي يسمعها، مهما كانت هادئة أو بعيدة.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Love your life, poor as it is.
quotes.translation: أحِبَّ حياتك، مهما كانت فقيرة.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Let every one mind his own business, and endeavor to be what he was made.
quotes.translation: ليهتمّ كلٌّ بشأنه، وليسعَ إلى أن يكون ما خُلق ليكونه.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Only that day dawns to which we are awake.
quotes.translation: لا يطلع إلا ذلك اليوم الذي نكون له يقظين.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Absolve you to yourself, and you shall have the suffrage of the world.
quotes.translation: برِّئ نفسك أمام نفسك، تنَل تأييد العالم.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds, adored by little statesmen and philosophers and divines.
quotes.translation: الاتساق الأحمق هو غول العقول الصغيرة، يعبده صغار الساسة والفلاسفة ورجال الدين.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Whoso would be a man must be a nonconformist.
quotes.translation: من أراد أن يكون رجلًا فعليه ألا يكون مقلِّدًا.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Every great man is an unique.
quotes.translation: كل عظيم فريد من نوعه.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Do that which is assigned thee, and thou canst not hope too much or dare too much.
quotes.translation: أدِّ ما أُسند إليك، ولن تكون مفرطًا في الأمل أو الجرأة.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Do your work, and you shall reinforce yourself.
quotes.translation: أنجز عملك، تَقْوَ بنفسك.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: We pass for what we are.
quotes.translation: نحن نُعرَف بما نحن عليه حقًا.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Your genuine action will explain itself and will explain your other genuine actions.
quotes.translation: فعلك الصادق يشرح نفسه، ويشرح أفعالك الصادقة الأخرى.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: The force of character is cumulative.
quotes.translation: قوة الشخصية تتراكم.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Greatness always appeals to the future.
quotes.translation: العظمة تخاطب المستقبل دائمًا.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Be it how it will, do right now.
quotes.translation: مهما يكن من أمر، افعل الصواب الآن.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: No law can be sacred to me but that of my nature.
quotes.translation: لا قانون مقدّس عندي إلا قانون طبيعتي.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Discontent is the want of self-reliance: it is infirmity of will.
quotes.translation: السخط هو نقص الاعتماد على النفس؛ إنه ضعف في الإرادة.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Let us, then, be up and doing, / With a heart for any fate; / Still achieving, still pursuing, / Learn to labor and to wait.
quotes.translation: فلننهض إذن ولنعمل، بقلب مستعد لأي قدر؛ نواصل الإنجاز والسعي، ونتعلم أن نكدّ وأن ننتظر.
quotes.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Act,— act in the living Present! / Heart within, and God o’erhead!
quotes.translation: اعمل، اعمل في الحاضر الحي! القلب في داخلك، والله فوقك!
quotes.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Be not like dumb, driven cattle! / Be a hero in the strife!
quotes.translation: لا تكن كالماشية الخرساء المسوقة! كن بطلًا في المعركة!
quotes.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: How dull it is to pause, to make an end, / To rust unburnish'd, not to shine in use!
quotes.translation: ما أبلد أن تتوقف، أن تضع نهاية، أن تصدأ غير مصقول بدل أن تلمع في الاستعمال!
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: To follow knowledge like a sinking star, / Beyond the utmost bound of human thought.
quotes.translation: أن تتبع المعرفة كنجم يهوي، إلى ما وراء أقصى حدود الفكر البشري.
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Made weak by time and fate, but strong in will / To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
quotes.translation: أضعفنا الزمن والقدر، لكننا أقوياء الإرادة: أن نسعى، ونبحث، ونجد، ولا نستسلم.
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: I am the master of my fate; / I am the captain of my soul.
quotes.translation: أنا سيّد قدري، أنا قائد روحي.
quotes.author: William Ernest Henley
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Under the bludgeoning of chance / My head is bloody, but unbowed.
quotes.translation: تحت ضربات الصدفة القاسية، رأسي دامٍ لكنه لا ينحني.
quotes.author: William Ernest Henley
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: Is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application?
quotes.translation: أليس من الممتع أن تتعلم بمثابرة واجتهاد دائمين؟
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.sourceNote: Public domain (author died long ago; translation pre-1929 where applicable). Copied from the linked page.

quotes.text: When you have faults, do not fear to abandon them.
